title: Supreme Court: LeDure v. Union Pacific Railroad Co.
summary: Judgment affirmed by an equally divided Court. (No. 20-807, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 596 U.S. 242).

title: Supreme Court: Cummings v. Premier Rehab Keller
summary: Emotional distress damages are not recoverable in a private action to enforce either the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 or the Affordable Care Act. (No. 20-219, opinion by Chief Justice Roberts; 596 U.S. 212).

title: Supreme Court: Boechler v. Commissioner
summary: The 30-day time limit to file a petition for review of a collection due process determination, 26 U. S. C. §6330(d)(1), is a nonjurisdictional deadline subject to equitable tolling. (No. 20-1472, opinion by Justice Barrett; 596 U.S. 199).

title: Supreme Court: United States v. Vaello Madero
summary: The Constitution does not require Congress to make Supplemental Security Income benefits available to residents of Puerto Rico. (No. 20-303, opinion by Justice Kavanaugh; 596 U.S. 159).

title: Supreme Court: Brown v. Davenport
summary: When a state court has ruled on the merits of a state prisoner’s claim, a federal court cannot grant habeas relief without applying both the test this Court outlined in Brecht v. Abrahamson, 507 U. S. 619, and the one Congress prescribed in the Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act of 1996; the Sixth Circuit erred in granting habeas relief to Mr. Davenport based solely on its assessment that he could satisfy the Brecht standard. (No. 20-826, opinion by Justice Gorsuch; 596 U.S. 118).

title: Supreme Court: Cassirer v. Thyssen-Bornemisza Collection Foundation
summary: In a suit raising non-federal claims against a foreign state or instrumentality under the Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act of 1976, a court should determine the substantive law by using the same choice-of-law rule applicable in a similar suit against a private party. (No. 20-1566, opinion by Justice Kagan; 596 U.S. 107).

title: Supreme Court: City of Austin v. Reagan National Advertising of Austin, LLC
summary: The distinction between on-premises signs and off-premises signs in the City of Austin’s sign code is facially content neutral under the First Amendment. (No. 20-1029, opinion by Justice Sotomayor; 596 U.S. 61).

title: Supreme Court: Thompson v. Clark
summary: Petitioner Thompson’s showing that his criminal prosecution ended without a conviction satisfies the requirement to demonstrate a favorable termination of a criminal prosecution in a Fourth Amendment claim under 42 U. S. C. §1983 for malicious prosecution; an affirmative indication of innocence is not needed. (No. 20-659, opinion by Justice Kavanaugh; 596 U.S. 36).
